metadata:curate:
I wrote `/Users/gapp/Desktop/Piano/catalog/metadata.json`. It has 69 entries in file-name order with unique ids, and every field the task asked for. No other project file was changed; the generator scripts are in `/tmp/pinspect`.

I used 3 quick web searches for composer facts, since you said to use public info. For duplicates, I compared the notes in each pair measure by measure.

**Judgment calls:**

1. **Composers corrected from public info:**
   - **Mariage d'Amour (3 files):** composer is Paul de Senneville. The two files whose credits say "Spring Waltz" are titled `Mariage d'Amour ("Spring Waltz")`.
   - **G Minor Bach (2 files):** composer is Luo Ni, not J.S. Bach. It is a modern rework of Bach's Prelude BWV 847, and the two files' notes match about 99%.
   - **Carol of the Bells (2 files):** composer is Mykola Leontovych. William J. Ross, who sits in the composer slot, is treated as the arranger.
   - **Hungarian Sonata:** I kept Richard Clayderman, as the file credits him. Many sources name Paul de Senneville, but I found no authoritative source, so it's only mentioned in the notes.
   - **Files with no composer credit** (Fur_Elise_Easy_Piano, Happy_Birthday_To_You_Piano, the uncredited K. 545 file): the composer comes from the title, and the attribution says the file doesn't name one.

2. **Suspected duplicates (13).** In each pair I flagged the copy with weaker credits or the later date:
   - **Exact or near-exact (99–100%):** Passacaglia, the E minor Prélude, Rondo alla Turca fingered, Für Elise fingered, Minuet in G, K. 545, Moonlight 3rd movement, G Minor Bach.
   - **97%:** Clair de lune, and Spring_Waltz_Mariage_dAmour after allowing for one inserted measure.
   - **94%:** Chopin_-_Spring_Waltz.
   - **Gymnopédie:** the 47-measure file uses a repeat, and each of its measures matches the written-out 78-measure file exactly.
   - **Not on your candidate list:** the two C♯ minor Nocturnes (82% match, same 65 measures). The differences are mostly trills and how the fast runs are written.
   - **The Entertainer is not flagged.** The Rui Sousa file has about 24% fewer notes (thinner chords, single bass notes instead of octaves), so I called it a "lightly simplified edition" rather than a duplicate.

3. **Overrides:**
   - **Ballade:** P2 is left out. Its 3 notes in measure 7 are an alternative chord (D on top instead of E♭) for a beat P1 already plays.
   - **G_Minor_Bach.mxl:** P1 is left out. Its 10 notes are a written-out trill in measures 21–22 on top of notes P2 already plays.
   - **The Entertainer (Rui Sousa) and Schubert Serenade:** P1 is the right hand and P2 the left. Entertainer P1 is above P2 in 89 of 90 measures. Serenade P1 is higher in 106 of 110, and the hands cross in measures 40, 41, 53 and 59.

4. **License notes (24).** These cover:
   - rights lines that name someone or something (©, 2016, jvs, websites, a person's name);
   - named modern arrangers, including usernames like lemontart, Nohpets and TheoA;
   - copyrighted modern pieces (Mariage d'Amour, G Minor Bach, Hungarian Sonata);
   - the 2014 Rui Sousa edition.

   Unnamed arrangers get no license note, as the rules say, although those arrangements may also be copyrighted.

5. **Other calls:**
   - **Twinkle:** described as "Mozart's own theme and 12 variations (credited 'arr. Solángel')", because the content matches K. 265.
   - **"Rev. John German":** kept as "rev." because it's unclear whether it means revised or Reverend.
   - **Danse villageoise:** kept as "No. 2" with no WoO number. Public sources only tentatively link the title to WoO 11.
   - **Arrangement wording:** Bach and Petzold keyboard pieces say "Original keyboard work". Toccata, Beethoven 5, Air, Swan Lake and Waltz of the Flowers mention the original organ or orchestral version.
   - **Wrong keys in file names:** noted for Waltz Op. 64 No. 2 and Nocturne No. 20 (say "C Minor", are C♯ minor) and Liebestraum (says "A Major", is A♭ major).
   - **Automatic notes:** each file also gets notes for pickup bars, repeats and 1st/2nd endings, D.S. al Coda, fingering, chord symbols, and 10 or more hidden playback-only notes. I removed the pickup note from Gnossienne because it is written in free time.
   - **Ids:** generated directly from the file names, so they keep the names' typos (e.g. `prlude-…`, `gymnopdie-…`).
   - **Source URLs:** many files contain a MuseScore source URL in their metadata. I didn't add it as a field because it wasn't in the spec.

Sources:
- [Hungarian Sonata (Paul de Senneville) – YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YThVernEFqI)
- [Tomplay – Hungarian Sonata](https://tomplay.com/piano-sheet-music/clayderman-richard/hungarian-sonata-piano-score)
- [Piano Tiles wiki – G minor Bach](https://piano-tiles.fandom.com/wiki/G_minor_Bach)
- [Flat.io – G Minor Bach](https://flat.io/score/590907cc3a6db21ec87e926f-g-minor-bach)
- [Amazon.fr – Danse villageoise, WoO 11](https://www.amazon.fr/Danse-villageoise-Sieben-l%C3%A4ndlerische-Musiques/dp/B000WF7IF8)
